transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I really hope I'm not wasting your time with this. I know you have patients with much worse problems, but... well, my family thought I should come. 

I've just been feeling a bit tired lately. Actually, to be honest, it's... it's more than a bit. It's a little embarrassing to admit, because I don't want to sound lazy, but I'm just so worn out. Just doing simple things, like walking from the bedroom to the kitchen... it feels like I've been out hauling lumber all day. I try to rest, I really do, but sitting down or sleeping just doesn't give me anything back. 

I hope it's okay that I came in for that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, it's... it's been about four months now. I really hope I should have come in sooner, I just didn't want to make a fuss over nothing, you know? But yeah, around four months. It started right around the time my wife went back to working full-time. 

I've been... well, I'm not working right now, so I've been spending most of the weekdays alone at the house. I try to keep busy, I really do, but... I don't know, maybe I'm just not adjusting well to the quiet? Does that sound like something that could make a person this tired? I just want to make sure I'm explaining this right.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started feeling tired?

Well, um... I guess you could say that. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a good life and a wonderful wife, but... yeah. It's been pretty hard. 

I wake up and there's just this... this really heavy, hopeless feeling right here in my chest. I try to push past it, I really do, but... well, some days I end up just going out to the garage and sitting there. And, um, this is really embarrassing to admit, but sometimes I just cry. And I don't even know why, or what started it. I should be stronger than that, shouldn't I? I hope you don't think less of me for saying that. I just... I want to be honest with you so I can get better. Is it normal to feel that way?
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before you started feeling this way?

Well, um... that's a good question. I really try to keep up with things, I do. But, um... no, not really. 

I feel terrible about it, honestly. I used to love singing in the choir, and playing pickup basketball with the guys. And I was always out in the garage working on cars, or, you know, grilling out for the family on the weekends. But lately... I just can't seem to make myself care about any of it. I don't even answer people's texts anymore when they ask me to come out. 

I know I should, and I feel so guilty for letting people down. I don't want to seem like a bad friend or a bad husband. It's just... the energy isn't there, and the enjoyment isn't there. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as selfish or anything.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since you started feeling this way?

Well, um... weight? I haven't really noticed a big difference, to be honest. I mean, I haven't been stepping on the scale or anything, so I couldn't give you an exact number. 

My wife hasn't said anything about my clothes looking different, and I try to make sure I'm still eating when she cooks, so I don't worry her. I really don't want to add to her plate right now. But as far as I can tell, everything seems pretty much the same in that department. Is that... is it okay that I don't know for sure? Should I be keeping better track of that?
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?

Well, um... I really hate to admit this. I don't want you to think I'm crazy or, you know, ungrateful for everything I have. But... yes. 

It's really hard to say out loud. I feel so guilty even thinking it, because I know how much it would hurt my wife. But lately, this... this thought just keeps coming into my head that I should just be dead. That things would be easier for everyone if I wasn't here being such a burden. 

And, um... when I'm alone in the house, it actually really scares me. Because I start thinking that I might actually do something to make that happen. I try to push it away, I really do, but it just gets so loud sometimes. I hope you don't think I'm a terrible person for having those thoughts. I'm telling you because I want to get better, I promise. Is it... is it common for people to feel that way when they're struggling like this?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual or feeling like you're speeding up in your thoughts or actions?

Well, um... I guess I have noticed a change, but I try really hard not to let it show too much. I don't want people to think I'm being lazy or ignoring them. 

But, honestly... everything I do just feels so slow lately. It's like my whole body is moving through mud. Even simple things just take so much effort. And, um... when people talk to me, like my wife, I can hear what she's asking, but it just takes me such a long time to get the words out to answer her. I feel terrible about it, because I know it must be frustrating for her to wait on me. 

I really am trying my best to keep up, I promise. I just... I can't seem to make myself move any faster. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. Is it normal to feel that bogged down?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge most of the time since you started feeling this way?

Well, um... anxious? I wouldn't say I'm feeling on edge all the time, no. I mean, I try really hard to stay calm and not let things get to me. 

I know it's not good to be all wound up, and I really don't want to be difficult to be around. So I just try to take deep breaths and keep things peaceful, especially for my wife's sake. I don't think I've been overly nervous or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I know I'm struggling with the other stuff, but at least I'm not pacing the floors or feeling panicked. That's... that's okay, right? That I don't have that symptom?
Do you often feel worthless or guilty about things that wouldn't normally bother you?

Well, um... gosh, I really hate to admit this. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I know I shouldn't complain. But... yes, I do. 

I just... I keep thinking that I've completely failed my wife, and my kids, and my church. It's so embarrassing to say out loud. And the worst part—and I really hope you don't think I'm completely losing my mind when I say this—but it honestly feels like every bad thing happening around us lately is somehow... a punishment. Like I'm being punished for not being the man I was supposed to be for them. 

I try really hard to shake it off and be positive so I don't bring everyone else down, I promise I do. It just gets so heavy. Does... does that make sense to you? I hope I'm not sounding too terrible by admitting that. Is it normal to feel that kind of guilt when you're going through a rough patch?
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Well, um... restless? No, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to just stay put and not be a bother to anyone. 

Like I said before, everything just feels so slow and heavy, so I don't really have the energy to be fidgety or pace around. I mostly just sit in my chair. I try to stay out of my wife's way so she doesn't have to worry about me being restless or getting into things. 

I hope that's alright? I mean, I know I'm not doing much of anything these days, but at least I'm not being disruptive or hyper, right? I really do try to just keep quiet and still. Is it... is it better that I'm not feeling restless on top of everything else?
Have you had any difficulty concentrating or making decisions since you started feeling this way?

Well, um... concentrating? I mean, maybe a little bit, but I really try my best to stay focused. I don't want to be one of those people who just spaces out when someone is talking to them. I know how rude that can be.

I guess... sometimes when my wife asks me what I want for dinner, or what we should watch on TV, I just tell her whatever she wants is fine. It's not that I can't decide, exactly, it's just... I want her to be happy, you know? And honestly, my mind does wander a bit when I try to read the paper lately. 

But I'm really trying to pay attention, especially when she needs me. I hope I'm not being too much of a burden by being a little forgetful or indecisive. It's not terrible, though, I promise. I can still hold a conversation, like we are now, right? I'm doing okay with your questions?
Are there any activities that you still find yourself looking forward to?

Well, um... gosh, I really wish I could say yes. I know how important it is to keep busy and have hobbies, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just giving up or being lazy. 

I used to have lots of things I loved. I always looked forward to choir practice, and playing pickup ball with the guys. I liked working on cars in the garage, and... well, I was always the one grilling for the family on the weekends. I really tried to be involved and do things for everyone. 

But lately... I'm so embarrassed to admit this, because I know it makes me sound like a terrible friend and father... I just can't make myself care enough to do any of it. I don't even show up anymore. The guys will text me about a game or choir, and I... I can't even bring myself to answer their texts. I just leave them hanging. 

It's awful of me, I know. I feel so guilty about it. I really hope they don't think I'm just being rude or ignoring them on purpose. Do you think... I mean, is it common to just lose your spark like that? I'm really hoping to get back to being the guy who grills and sings for them, I promise I am. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for letting all that slide right now.
Have you been feeling like you need to be in constant motion or have an inability to sit still?

Well, um... no, not at all. I think that might be... well, kind of like what you asked a few minutes ago? About being restless? 

I promise I'm not bouncing off the walls or anything like that. I really don't feel any urge to be up and moving. Like I mentioned, I mostly just stay right in my chair all day. I try to be very quiet and just stay out of the way. I definitely don't have any trouble sitting still. 

I hope it's alright that my answer is the same for that? I know you have a list of things you need to ask, and I really want to give you the right information. I'm trying my best to be a good patient for you... I'm answering everything okay, aren't I?
Are there any small pleasures in life that you still enjoy, like tasting your favorite food or taking a warm bath?

Well, um... I know we sort of just talked about this a little bit, when I mentioned the choir and the grilling and all that. I really, really wish I could give you a different answer this time. I want to be able to tell you that a nice meal or a warm bath makes a difference, because I know I should be grateful for those little things. I really try not to be a complainer, and I don't want to sound unappreciative of what I have. 

But... it's just like I was saying before, about not even being able to answer my friends' texts anymore. I just can't make myself care about any of it, even the small stuff. The spark is just... gone. 

I feel terrible saying that. I'm sorry to just give you the same kind of bad news again, especially when you're trying so hard to help me find something positive. I hope I'm not frustrating you by repeating myself. I'm really doing my best to think of something for you... is it okay that my answer is kind of the same?
Do you feel like your depression is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

Well, um... I guess I'd have to say it's... it's probably severe. I really don't like using that word, because I know there are people out there who have it so much worse than I do, and I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or making a big deal out of nothing. 

But... just with how I can't even get out of my chair, and how I've let everyone down... I think it's pretty bad right now. I hope it doesn't make me sound weak to say that. I really am trying to be strong and push through it, I promise. I just... I want to be honest with you so you can help me. Is that the right way to describe it? I hope I'm making sense.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things that might happen in the future?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, I try not to. I know worrying doesn't actually fix anything, and I really don't want to be one of those people who's always fretting and making everyone around them anxious, you know? 

I mostly just... well, like I said, I sit in my chair and try to stay quiet. I don't really think too much about what's coming next because... well, I guess I just don't see much of a future to worry about right now. 

I hope that doesn't sound too negative. I know I should be more forward-thinking and trying to plan how to get better. I really am trying to be cooperative, I promise. Is it okay that I don't have a lot of worries like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of answers you need.
Have you been feeling an internal restlessness that makes you want to move around or engage in activities?

Well, um... no, not really. I don't think I've felt anything like that. I mostly just... well, like I mentioned, I pretty much just sit in my chair most of the day. 

I really hope that's an okay answer. I know it probably sounds like I'm just being lazy, not wanting to get up and do things. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or avoid being active. It's just... I don't really have that urge to move around or do much of anything right now. 

I feel bad saying that, because I know exercise and moving around is supposed to be good for you. I really should try harder to get up more. I hope you don't think poorly of me for just sitting there so much... is it alright that I don't have that restless feeling you're asking about?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there are any activities the patient still looks forward to, which directly assesses for anhedonia or loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities.

patient.answer:
Well, um... gosh, I really wish I could say yes. I know how important it is to keep busy and have hobbies, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just giving up or being lazy. 

I used to have lots of things I loved. I always looked forward to choir practice, and playing pickup ball with the guys. I liked working on cars in the garage, and... well, I was always the one grilling for the family on the weekends. I really tried to be involved and do things for everyone. 

But lately... I'm so embarrassed to admit this, because I know it makes me sound like a terrible friend and father... I just can't make myself care enough to do any of it. I don't even show up anymore. The guys will text me about a game or choir, and I... I can't even bring myself to answer their texts. I just leave them hanging. 

It's awful of me, I know. I feel so guilty about it. I really hope they don't think I'm just being rude or ignoring them on purpose. Do you think... I mean, is it common to just lose your spark like that? I'm really hoping to get back to being the guy who grills and sings for them, I promise I am. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for letting all that slide right now.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of psychomotor agitation
doctor.question: Have you been feeling like you need to be in constant motion or have an inability to sit still?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychomotor agitation (feeling the need to be in constant motion or inability to sit still). My symptom profile includes Psychomotor Changes (S028), but my manifestation specifically describes psychomotor retardation (slowing down, moving through mud), not agitation. Therefore, I do not have the specific symptom of constant motion/inability to sit still.

patient.answer:
Well, um... no, not at all. I think that might be... well, kind of like what you asked a few minutes ago? About being restless? 

I promise I'm not bouncing off the walls or anything like that. I really don't feel any urge to be up and moving. Like I mentioned, I mostly just stay right in my chair all day. I try to be very quiet and just stay out of the way. I definitely don't have any trouble sitting still. 

I hope it's alright that my answer is the same for that? I know you have a list of things you need to ask, and I really want to give you the right information. I'm trying my best to be a good patient for you... I'm answering everything okay, aren't I?

doctor.question: Are there any small pleasures in life that you still enjoy, like tasting your favorite food or taking a warm bath?

patient.answer:
Well, um... I know we sort of just talked about this a little bit, when I mentioned the choir and the grilling and all that. I really, really wish I could give you a different answer this time. I want to be able to tell you that a nice meal or a warm bath makes a difference, because I know I should be grateful for those little things. I really try not to be a complainer, and I don't want to sound unappreciative of what I have. 

But... it's just like I was saying before, about not even being able to answer my friends' texts anymore. I just can't make myself care about any of it, even the small stuff. The spark is just... gone. 

I feel terrible saying that. I'm sorry to just give you the same kind of bad news again, especially when you're trying so hard to help me find something positive. I hope I'm not frustrating you by repeating myself. I'm really doing my best to think of something for you... is it okay that my answer is kind of the same?

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Do you feel like your depression is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the subjective severity of the depression (mild, moderate, or severe). None of the symptom profile items directly address the subjective rating of severity; they describe specific symptoms like depressed mood, loss of interest, fatigue, etc. Therefore, there is no exact match for this question.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I guess I'd have to say it's... it's probably severe. I really don't like using that word, because I know there are people out there who have it so much worse than I do, and I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or making a big deal out of nothing. 

But... just with how I can't even get out of my chair, and how I've let everyone down... I think it's pretty bad right now. I hope it doesn't make me sound weak to say that. I really am trying to be strong and push through it, I promise. I just... I want to be honest with you so you can help me. Is that the right way to describe it? I hope I'm making sense.

inference.note: F32.0 and F32.1 were ruled out due to the patient's description of severe depression and loss of interest in activities, which suggests a more severe depressive episode.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's depression is accompanied by anxiety
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself worrying about things that might happen in the future?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about worrying about the future (anxiety), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Well, um... no, not really. I mean, I try not to. I know worrying doesn't actually fix anything, and I really don't want to be one of those people who's always fretting and making everyone around them anxious, you know? 

I mostly just... well, like I said, I sit in my chair and try to stay quiet. I don't really think too much about what's coming next because... well, I guess I just don't see much of a future to worry about right now. 

I hope that doesn't sound too negative. I know I should be more forward-thinking and trying to plan how to get better. I really am trying to be cooperative, I promise. Is it okay that I don't have a lot of worries like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of answers you need.

patient.answer:
Well, um... no, not really. I don't think I've felt anything like that. I mostly just... well, like I mentioned, I pretty much just sit in my chair most of the day. 

I really hope that's an okay answer. I know it probably sounds like I'm just being lazy, not wanting to get up and do things. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or avoid being active. It's just... I don't really have that urge to move around or do much of anything right now. 

I feel bad saying that, because I know exercise and moving around is supposed to be good for you. I really should try harder to get up more. I hope you don't think poorly of me for just sitting there so much... is it alright that I don't have that restless feeling you're asking about?
